title: Lighthouse Health - inference health, roadmap & orchestration sync
summary: Monthly health check focused on cost drift after recent rollout, reliability around long-tail latency, and roadmap alignment for canary/orchestration improvements. Agreed to run targeted perf benchmarks, share SOC2 + KMS docs, and refine cost model with real prefix caching assumptions.
topics: next QTR roadmap and pilot scope
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick confirmations, everyone can hear me?
[00:05] Tom Alvarez: Yeah can hear you, thanks Maya.
[00:09] Jordan Lee: good afternoon all, Jordan from Redwood here.
[00:12] Speaker 1 (Ravi?): uh yeah this is Ravi, we can hear you.
[00:18] Maya Patel: Cool. Goal for today is three things — cost spike post-launch, the latency tails we've been seeing on longer conversations, and roadmap bits around safer rollouts/orchestration. We'll go through usage dashboard then Q&A.
[00:30] Sara Kim: Quick note, last two weeks we pushed the predictive triage flow to 1m monthly active users which caused the token bump — so cost is up, and some 95/99th latency regressed.
[00:40] Priya Nambiar: Noted — we put notes in the ticket but wanted to walk through the numbers with you.
[00:45] [00:50] Jordan Lee: Okay can we pull up the per-route token breakdown? You're seeing which routes spiking?
[00:55] Ben Chu: It's mostly the multi-turn diagnostic flow, we have long histories and KV cache hit is lower than expected.
[01:05] Jordan Lee: Hmm uh KV cache — are you using prefix caching or full session caching?
[01:10] Sara Kim: We're only doing per-turn prefix caching right now; full session caching we haven't enabled because of privacy concerns and we thought it might blow memory.
[01:18] Jordan Lee: Right, so two levers: increase KV cache window (memory) or compress context with summarization before the call. That reduces tokens. We've seen 30–45% token drop in similar profiles.
[01:30] Tom Alvarez: Do you have a recommended config? We don't want to add to memory costs on Dedicated GPUs if we move that way.
[01:38] Jordan Lee: For long diagnostic sessions, we typically set KV cache retention to 6–8 steps for Llama-variant models and enable prefix dedupe + sparse attention if your model supports it. On hosted, Redwood can do that automatically; on Dedicated we can share a tuning guide.
[01:52] [02:00] Nadia Ortiz: Security question — if we compress context using server-side summarization, does that change PII handling or retention? We need the archived transcripts to match our compliance policy.
[02:10] Priya Nambiar: Good call Nadia. We'll share an example flow. Summaries can be configured to exclude PII or use PII redaction before storage; Redwood's Private deployments integrate with customer KMS so key control stays with you.
[02:25] Nadia Ortiz: Okay please send the SOC2 and KMS integration docs, we haven't fully validated the Private package.
[02:30] Maya Patel: We'll attach those — action item.
[02:34] [02:40] Tom Alvarez: Back to cost — our finance team flagged a 62% increase on the last invoice vs prior month. We expected some increase but not that much. The majority was generation tokens, correct?
[02:50] Jordan Lee: Based on the traces you shared, yes generation tokens are the driver. Two things: prompt expansion due to diagnostic transcripts, and retries/re-requests during timeouts.
[03:00] Sara Kim: About retrying — we did see a flurry of client-side retries after a few 504s during the rollout window. Our client library was aggressive.
[03:08] Priya Nambiar: We can help tune timeout/retry recommendations, and on Redwood side you can enable idempotency keys and automatic de-dup of near-duplicate requests.
[03:18] [03:30] Jordan Lee: Also recommend enabling adaptive batching for lower-cost background jobs; it won't help the low-latency user-facing route but will reduce cost on generation-heavy analytics.
[03:40] Ben Chu: Is the adaptive batching something we can control per-route?
[03:44] Jordan Lee: Yes per-route policy in the Console — you can set batch windows, burst thresholds. We'll send a sample policy.
[03:52] [04:00] Tom Alvarez: On reliability — our SREs noticed long tail is 700–1200ms where baseline is 150ms. It's mostly during peak windows. The error rate is low but latency spikes matter for UX.
[04:12] Jordan Lee: Right. Two paths: move latency-sensitive routes to Dedicated with pinned capacity, or keep hosted and use regional routing + smaller model variants for best-effort. Tradeoff is cost vs fidelity.
[04:26] Maya Patel: Redwood's smart routing can fallback to quantized variants during capacity pressure — that keeps availability but can change outputs. Did you see quality degradation when fallbacks happened?
[04:38] Sara Kim: Users reported subtle changes in answer phrasing, not accuracy issues per se, but product team worried about consistency.
[04:46] Jordan Lee: We can set deterministic model pins for critical routes while allowing noncritical flows to use fallbacks. Also there are ephemeral model mappings for canary rollouts so only a percentage of users hit the new model.
[04:58] [05:10] Ravi Desai: About canaries — we need safer orchestration. We had an incident where the canary criteria was too lenient and rolled out to 30% before rollback. Can Redwood do automatic rollback on metrics deviation?
[05:20] Evan Torres: Yes, Redwood Optimize supports metric-based rollbacks — tie the canary to latency/response-quality sag and configure automatic rollback thresholds. We'll need SLO metrics from your side to wire into the policy.
[05:32] Tom Alvarez: We have a custom quality metric (Q-Score) from our eval harness. Can that integrate?
[05:36] Jordan Lee: Absolutely — you can emit Q-Score via tracing hooks, Redwood Console will ingest and evaluate canaries on it.
[05:42] [06:00] Speaker 2 (Ben?): small aside, any thoughts on moving to VPC private deployment for PHI workloads?
[06:06] Priya Nambiar: Private is the recommended path for PHI. You get customer-managed networking, KMS integration, and audit log streaming. There are on-prem options if you need air-gapped.
[06:17] Nadia Ortiz: How long is the onboarding for Private? We've budgeted a quarter if needed.
[06:22] Maya Patel: Typical timeline is 6–10 weeks for VPC-based Private (provisioning, network setup, security review) and 12+ weeks for on-prem depending on infra approvals. We'll share a template plan.
[06:35] [06:50] Sara Kim: For now we want to avoid full Private because of velocity; can we get near-PHI posture by using hosted plus VPC peering and strict KMS?
[06:58] Jordan Lee: There's a middle ground — dedicated capacity with VPC peering + customer KMS and restricted data retention. It gives many of the compliance controls without full Private. We'll map exactly which controls line up with your policy.
[07:12] [07:30] Tom Alvarez: Let's talk concrete next steps. We need a refined cost model that includes prefix cache hit-rate assumptions, retry reduction, and potential Dedicated pricing. Also need perf runs to reproduce the 99th tail.
[07:44] Jordan Lee: Agreed — we can run bench jobs from your sample traces at three configurations: hosted baseline, hosted with prefix compression + dedupe, and Dedicated pinned capacity. We'll model cost per 1m sessions.
[07:58] Maya Patel: We'll scope that as a pilot, Redwood will own the runs and share results in 10 business days.
[08:06] [08:20] Ben Chu: Anything else from customer side?
[08:24] Sara Kim: We want an updated rollout strategy doc for canaries with examples of threshold values and a sample automation script.
[08:32] Priya Nambiar: We'll share the rollout playbook and a ready-to-run policy you can drop into your pipeline.
[08:36] [08:45] Tom Alvarez: On finance — can you give a breakdown of invoice line-items so our accounting can map them? They asked for per-route token breakdown, Dedicated commit amortization, and overage events.
[08:56] Maya Patel: We'll provide a spreadsheet with per-route token math and a model for amortized commit.
[09:02] Jordan Lee: Also suggest enabling per-token tracing for a short window to help attribute token sources. That will increase logging but for one week it helps root cause.
[09:12] [09:30] Speaker 1 (Ravi?): small merchant, are competitors like Anthropic/Vertex relevant here?
[09:36] Maya Patel: We sometimes see customers compare cost on Vertex or Anthropic; for your long multi-turn flows the main differentiators will be batching, KV cache effectiveness, and rollout controls. We'll include competitive notes.
[09:48] [10:00] Priya Nambiar: Quick recap — action items and owners at the end. Anything else?
[10:05] Nadia Ortiz: One security ask: can Redwood provide an example SOC2 APL for hosted and one for Private?
[10:12] Maya Patel: Yes.
[10:18] [10:30] Jordan Lee: Okay I'll summarize the technical plan: 1) run perf benchmarks with your traces across three configs, 2) test cache/window configs and summarization to cut tokens, 3) demo canary rollback automation with Q-Score integration.
[10:45] Tom Alvarez: Perfect.
[10:50] Maya Patel: Great thanks everyone. We'll follow up with timeline and docs.
[10:55] [11:00] END OF TRANSCRIPT
